title: Compare two runs by per-case transition
problem: An aggregate that moves from 41 to 43 passing cases hides the case that broke. The question a user actually has is which cases changed and in which direction, and an aggregate cannot answer it.
context: Builds on immutable run records. The comparison reads two existing records and writes nothing to them.
impact: This is the output the tool exists to produce. Everything before it is plumbing.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The comparison reports per-case transitions covering at minimum became-passing, became-failing, unchanged, added and removed.
Transitions into and out of errored are reported distinctly from transitions into and out of failed.
A case present in one run and absent from the other is reported as added or removed, never silently dropped and never counted as a change in outcome.
A comparison against an unknown run id reports which id was not found and lists the ids that exist. It never falls back to the nearest run.
Comparison does not modify either record. Both are byte-identical afterwards.
Automated tests cover every transition kind including the errored transitions, a differing population, and an unknown run id. All pass at the submitted revision.
The learner explains how a case present in only one run is handled, one rejected alternative, and one comparison this output could still mislead a reader about.

constraints: Standard library plus a test runner only.
No statistical testing, confidence intervals or significance claims.
Comparison is read-only with respect to run records.
Do not push to a remote or open a pull request as part of this task.

scope.description: A pure function over two records and its presentation.

investigation_areas: What the transition set should be, and whether the five named ones are sufficient
How a differing case population is represented without implying an outcome change
What an honest summary line says when most cases errored
testing_expectations: Run the project's own test suite. State the exact command in the design.
documentation_requirements: Record the transition taxonomy and the rejected alternative in the learner design.
